title: RNA Extraction from Sterivex Filters
author: William Brazelton
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bykspuwe
materials: Gently shake a few times and centrifuge.
Add salt solutions: RNA : 0.5x volumes of ammonium acetate (7.5 M) (ex: 125 μL to 250 μL) DNA : 0.1 volumes of sodium acetate (3M, pH 5.2). (ex: 40 μL to 400 μL)
Invert a few times to mix.

Nucleic Acid Extraction Buffer (NEB): 0.1M Tris-HCl (pH 8) 4.5 mL of 1.0 M 0.1M Na-EDTA (pH 8) 9 mL of 0.5M 0.1M KH2PO4 (pH 8) 0.54 g 1.5M NaCl 13.5 mL of 5M 0.8M Guanidine HCl 3.44 g 0.5% Triton-X 100 225 μL of 100% Add above ingredients to 50 mL tube. Add UltraPure water to ~40 mL Add NaOH to pH ~7 (slowly) Add UltraPure water to 45 mL Filter sterilize with 0.22 μm filter Autoclave with lid loosened. Recover from autoclave soon after the cycle is complete. Pour autoclaved solution into fresh 50 mL tube. Aliquot into 1.5 mL tubes. UV sterilize for 10-30 minutes.

steps.title: Initial Filter Treatment
steps.instruction: Add 1.4 mL of NEB to each Sterivex filter using a syringe and needle.

substeps.instruction: Position the needle just below the mouth of the Sterivex so it does not come back out the top.
Stop filling when the solution covers the filter; do not fill to the top.

steps.title: Incubation and Lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the filters at room temperature for 30 minutes, then vortex each Sterivex (inside a Falcon tube) for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Fluid Recovery and Bead Treatment
steps.instruction: Withdraw fluid from each Sterivex using a syringe and eject it into a bead tube (glass 0.1 mm for bacteria).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge for 2 min at 5000 g.
Transfer fluid into a fresh 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, avoiding the beads.
Ensure no more than 350 μL is added per tube.

steps.title: RNA Extraction (Phenol/Chloroform)
steps.instruction: Perform acid phenol/chloroform extraction to isolate RNA from the lysates.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of acid phenol/chloroform (pH 5.2) to each tube.
Gently shake a few times and centrifuge at 14,000g for 1 minute.
Remove 300 μL of supernatant to a fresh tube, avoiding the organic phase and interface.
Repeat phenol extraction until the interface is clear.
Retain the tube containing the organic phase for potential DNA recovery.

steps.title: RNA Purification (Chloroform/Isoamyl Alcohol)
steps.instruction: Further purify the RNA aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to each tube.
Carefully remove the supernatant to a fresh tube, avoiding the bottom organic layer.
Redistribute the aqueous phase into tubes (250 μL per tube for RNA).
Add 2.5x volumes of 100% ethanol (e.g., 937.5 μL ethanol to 375 μL sample).
Incubate at -20ºC for at least 1 hour or overnight (alternatively, incubation on ice may yield a cleaner pellet).
Centrifuge for 40 minutes at 16,000g (optionally use a cooled centrifuge at 0ºC).

steps.title: RNA Pellet Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet to remove residual salts.

substeps.instruction: Pour out the supernatant, keeping the tube at a gentle angle to prevent the pellet from falling out.
Add 500 μL of cold 70% ethanol to each tube.
Invert the tube to mix and ensure the pellet is dislodged from the bottom.
Centrifuge at 16,000g for 10 minutes.
Remove the liquid with a pipettor, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: RNA Drying and Resuspension
steps.instruction: Dry and resuspend the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes with open lids in the UV hood until ethanol has evaporated but pellets remain damp (do not let them become powdery).
Resuspend the pellet in 50-100 μL of UltraPure water and pipette to mix.
If the pellet does not readily dissolve, incubate at 55ºC for 30-60 seconds (avoid prolonged heating to prevent degradation).

steps.title: DNA Extraction from Original Lysates
steps.instruction: Recover DNA from the original lysate tubes.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 μL UltraPure Water to the original tubes and shake gently to mix.
Add an equal volume (of total volume) of phenol/chloroform (pH 8.0) to each tube.
Gently shake a few times and centrifuge at 14,000g for 1 minute.
Remove the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (24:1) to each tube.
Carefully remove the supernatant to a fresh tube, avoiding the bottom organic layer.
Redistribute the aqueous phase into tubes (400 μL per tube for DNA).
Add 2.0 volumes of 100% ethanol (e.g., 880 μL ethanol to 440 μL sample).
Incubate at -20ºC for at least 1 hour or overnight (or on ice).
Centrifuge for 40 minutes at 16,000g (optionally at 0ºC).
Pour out supernatant at a gentle angle.
Wash with 500 μL cold 70% ethanol: invert to mix, centrifuge at 16,000g for 10 minutes, and remove liquid.
Dry pellets in the UV hood until ethanol evaporates but pellets remain damp.

steps.title: DNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in low EDTA TE or EB buffer.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend in 50-100 μL of low EDTA TE (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 0.1 mM EDTA) or EB (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8 or 8.5).
Heat to 55ºC for 10 or more minutes to dissolve the pellet.

steps.title: Storage and Downstream Processing
steps.instruction: Store or convert the extracted nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: Convert RNA to cDNA immediately and store remaining RNA at -80ºC.
Store cDNA working aliquots at 4ºC (short term) or -20ºC/-80ºC (long term).
Store DNA working aliquots at 4ºC and archive samples at -20ºC or -80ºC.
Avoid repeated freeze/thaw cycles for both RNA and DNA.
